stem: Butan-2-ol is treated with Lucas reagent, concentrated HCl and anhydrous ZnCl$_2$. Which product causes the turbidity?

verdicts.working: Butan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol; Lucas reagent converts it to 2-chlorobutane, whose separation causes turbidity.

working:
Butan-2-ol + HCl $\xrightarrow{\text{ZnCl}_2}$ 2-chlorobutane + H$_2$O
The insoluble alkyl chloride forms droplets, causing turbidity.

Independent check: Butan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol; Lucas reagent converts it to 2-chlorobutane, whose separation causes turbidity.
solution:
Lucas reagent converts the secondary alcohol to the corresponding alkyl chloride:
$$\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH)CH_2CH_3 + HCl \xrightarrow{ZnCl_2} CH_3CH(Cl)CH_2CH_3 + H_2O}$$
Insoluble 2-chlorobutane separates as droplets, causing turbidity.
